user.title: AI models
user.description: Which AI Task entities look at each camera frame, in order. Each model is tried only when the one before gives no answer (busy, error or out of quota).

data_description.first_look: Runs on every sighting. Put the main model first and backups after it.
data_description.second_opinion: Double-checks priority animals, strict animals, unknown cats and unsure answers. Use different models from the first look.
data_description.paid_models: Models that cost money. They are labelled "last resort" and are never used in independent shadow mode. Put them last in each list.
data_description.main_start: Optional: use the first model in the first-look list only between these times, to save its daily quota for the busiest hours. Backups cover the rest of the night.
data_description.main_end: Leave both empty to use it all night.

schedule.title: When to watch
schedule.description: Cameras are watched between these times, and also whenever the sun is down if you turn that on (whichever is wider).

data.use_dark: Also watch whenever it is dark

data_description.summary_time: Last night's summary is built at this time each morning, and a new night starts.
data_description.on_camera_minutes: How long an animal shows as on camera after a sighting.
data_description.watch_always: For daytime visitors too. Every check uses AI quota, so this uses more.

cameras.title: Cameras
cameras.description: Pick the cameras to watch. Each one is set up on the next pages, filled in from its own device. You can add more later with Add camera.

camera.title: Camera: {camera}
camera.description: Motion and animal sensors trigger a check; person and vehicle sensors skip it. Check the suggestions.

data.name: Name
data.triggers: Start a check when any of these turn on
data.skip_when: Skip the check while any of these are on
data.reopened_by: A check on these cameras ends the cooldown
data.ai_notes: What the AI should know about this view

data_description.name: Used in the AI prompt, alerts and the summary, e.g. Garage.
data_description.cooldown: Minimum time between checks of this camera.
data_description.priority_cooldown: Used instead when this camera's last real animal was a priority animal. 0 = off.
data_description.missing_cooldown: Used instead while any missing mode is on. 0 = off.
data_description.reopened_by: For a camera an animal passes on its way here.
data_description.deterrent_lights: Turned on when a pest (wildlife set to scare off) is seen here, then back off.
data_description.deterrent_sound: Played when a pest is seen here.
data_description.check_every: For a camera without a motion sensor (any RTSP / ONVIF camera): look on a timer. 0 = only when a sensor triggers. Uses AI quota on every check.
data_description.ai_notes: Only this camera's checks see it. E.g. the bins are at the left; a cat behind the window on the right is an indoor pet.

animal.title: Animals
animal.description: Describe each animal the AI should recognise. {count} added so far. Leave the name empty to finish; you can add more later with Add animal.

data.name: Name
data.add_another: Add another animal after this one

data_description.description: Sent to the AI. Lead with the markings that still show in infrared at night.
data_description.tips: Extra rules for telling this animal apart, e.g. what it is never confused with.
data_description.pattern: For a priority animal, both AI models must report this pattern.
data_description.base: The tone covering more than half the body. For a priority animal, both AI models must report it.
data_description.priority: Never missed, never falsely confirmed: high confidence needs both AI models to agree and to see its coat. Adds missing mode and a confirmed-on-camera signal.
data_description.always_strict: Counts only when both AI models name it at high confidence. Animals not seen for a while are strict automatically.
data_description.reference_upload: A clear night photo, sent to the AI beside each frame.
data_description.known_last_seen: Optional: when it was last seen, if you know (e.g. from an earlier setup). Animals not seen for a while are treated as recently absent.
data_description.known_location: Optional: where it was last seen.
data_description.alert_at: Cameras where it sends an alert. Empty: never.
data_description.critical_at: Where its Critical alerts switch makes it ring through silent mode. Empty: wherever it alerts.

wildlife.title: Pests
wildlife.description: Which animals are pests? Pests alert every time they come back and can be scared off with a camera's lights and sound. Every other animal is still recognised and tracked as wildlife, with no setup.

people.title: Who gets alerts
people.description: These phones get Neighborhood Watch alerts. Quiet zones (like work), sounds and missing-mode alerts can be set per person afterwards.

error.first_look_required: Pick at least one model for the first look.
error.priority_not_strict: A priority animal has its own stricter rules; turn off Always strict.

abort.no_ai_task: Set up an AI Task integration first (for example Google Generative AI).

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: Shadow modes never fire the sighting event, so nothing alerts or feeds. Compare results with the Shadow mismatches sensor.

models.title: AI models
models.description: Each model is tried only when the one before gives no answer.

data_description.first_look: Runs on every sighting. Main model first, backups after it.
data_description.second_opinion: Double-checks priority animals, strict animals, unknown cats and unsure answers.
data_description.paid_models: Labelled "last resort"; never used in independent shadow mode.
data_description.main_start: Optional: use the first model in the first-look list only between these times, to save its daily quota for the busiest hours. Backups cover the rest of the night.
data_description.main_end: Leave both empty to use it all night.

data.use_dark: Also watch whenever it is dark

data_description.watch_always: For daytime visitors too. Every check uses AI quota, so this uses more.

identification.title: Identification
identification.description: The AI instructions. {animals} is replaced with each animal's description, {location} with the camera name, {absent} with the recently-absent line, {extra_rules} with the extra rules and {wildlife} with the wildlife list.

data_description.extra_rules: Rules for every camera. Notes about one camera go on that camera's page.
data_description.wildlife: Animals you often see, as hints. Not a limit: the AI names whatever it sees, and corrections accept any animal.
data_description.absent_days: An animal not seen this long is named only when both AI models are sure.
data_description.reference_photos: Each animal's reference photo goes to the AI beside the frame. More accurate; uses more tokens.

notifications.title: Notification pictures
notifications.description: Each sighting event carries a picture link that phones can open. Leave empty to use this Home Assistant's external URL.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.description: Who gets alerts is set per person (Add person). Cameras, animals and wildlife each decide when they alert.

data_description.alerts: Turn off if your own automations send the alerts (they can use the sighting event).
data_description.correction_buttons: Tap to confirm or correct a sighting. Corrections fix tracking and label the training data.
data_description.min_confidence: Less sure answers don't alert; they wait in the review queue. Critical alerts and missing mode ignore this.

training.title: Training data
training.description: Every checked frame is saved, downscaled, with what the AI said and what you confirmed or corrected. It is what a custom model is trained on.

data_description.dataset_dir: Leave empty for the media folder. A network share (e.g. a NAS added under Settings → System → Storage) keeps it off this device.
data_description.dataset_gb: When full, the oldest unlabelled frames go first; labelled ones are kept longest.

detector.title: Local detector
detector.description: An optional MegaDetector service on your own machine (see the vision folder in the repository). It looks at every frame before the AI. Start with Shadow and watch the Detector agreement sensor; switch to Skip empty frames once it has no misses.

data_description.detector_url: e.g. {example}. Leave empty to turn it off.
data_description.detector_min: Below this confidence the frame counts as empty.

catch_alls.title: Wildlife and catch-alls
catch_alls.description: Every animal that isn't one of yours is recognised and tracked as wildlife, without adding it. Pests are the kinds you list here; everything else is other wildlife. Unknown animals: a cat or dog that isn't one of yours. Unsure motion: the AI saw movement but couldn't say what.

data.unknown_critical_at: Unknown animals: critical alerts only at
data.other_critical_at: Other wildlife: critical alerts only at
data.motion_critical_at: Unsure motion: critical alerts only at

data_description.pests: Alert every time they come back, and are scared off with a camera's lights and sound.
data_description.motion_critical_at: Each has a Critical alerts switch on the Neighborhood Watch device; these limit where it rings. Empty: wherever it alerts.

options.shadow_reuse: Shadow, reuse answers: re-run the rules on another system's sighting events (no AI calls)
options.shadow_independent: Shadow, independent: check cameras itself without paid models

options.shadow: Shadow: ask it and compare, change nothing
options.skip_empty: Skip empty frames: no AI call when it finds no animal (never in missing mode)

options.normal: Critical alerts arrive as normal ones

no_photo.message: There is no photo of that animal yet; name a camera to take one now.

note_needs_target.message: Choose a camera or an animal for the note.

identify.name: Identify
identify.description: Checks a camera now, ignoring its cooldown, and returns what the AI found.

test_sighting.name: Test sighting
test_sighting.description: Fires a fake sighting event marked test, so you can check your alerts. Tracking is never changed.

priority_candidate.name: Priority candidate
priority_candidate.description: Whether either AI named a priority animal. Auto = yes only when the animal is one.

mark_wrong.name: Mark wrong
mark_wrong.description: Removes the latest counted sighting of an animal from tracking, e.g. that wasn't Pepper.

animal.name: Animal
animal.description: The animal that was named wrongly.

camera.name: Camera
camera.description: Only the latest sighting at this camera.

set_reference_photo.name: Set reference photo
set_reference_photo.description: Uses the animal's last photo as its reference photo, or takes one from a camera now.

camera.name: Camera
camera.description: Take a fresh snapshot from this camera instead.

build_summary.name: Build night summary
build_summary.description: Builds the night summary now and starts a new night.

correct.name: Correct a sighting
correct.description: Confirms or corrects what a camera saw. Tracking and the photo move to the right animal, and the training frame is labelled.

answer.name: Answer
answer.description: right, wrong, unsure (looked at, no verdict), or what it really was (an animal's name, a wildlife kind, or nothing).

sighting_id.name: Sighting
sighting_id.description: The sighting's id (from an alert or Last detection). Empty = the latest one.

camera.name: Camera
camera.description: Without an id: the latest sighting at this camera.

scan.name: Scan a folder
scan.description: Bulk-scans photos and videos in a folder on the local detector's machine. The detector finds each animal visit, the AI names it, and a report is written into the folder. Visits also join the review queue.

folder.name: Folder
folder.description: A folder inside the detector's scan folder, e.g. trailcam/2026-10.

identify.name: Name the animals
identify.description: Ask the AI what each visit is (uses AI quota: one or two calls per visit).

limit.name: At most
limit.description: How many visits to name; the rest are listed as "animal".

add_note.name: Add a note for the AI
add_note.description: Adds a note where the AI will use it: a camera's view notes, or an animal's identification tips.

camera.name: Camera
camera.description: Add it to this camera's view notes.

animal.name: Animal
animal.description: Or add it to this animal's (or wildlife kind's) tips.

move_training_data.name: Move training data
move_training_data.description: Moves saved training photos into the current training folder, e.g. after pointing it at a NAS.

from.name: From
from.description: Folders to move from. Empty: the default folder in the media folder.
